statements.quote: In the context of providing medical care, physicians will see people with this problem.
statements.context: Essay on factitious disorder by proxy (Munchausen by proxy). The author says the condition is rare on a population basis but that physicians in clinical practice will encounter it. Habitual, generic 'will'.
statements.note: Borderline. Habitual 'will' describing a standing pattern, not a dated future state. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: She isn’t stopping, she isn’t apologizing, and she won’t be bullied into pretending Mr. Bitey isn’t cool.
statements.context: Personal essay about the author's seven-year-old daughter Quinn and her stuffed snowman character Mr. Bitey. Peers at school mock her fixation; the author expects she will not be bullied out of it.
statements.note: Personal character statement about the author's daughter, not a domain forecast. Logged as borderline.

statements.quote: conveying the true characteristics of randomness in psychiatric education might help clinicians better identify when a trend in their clinical experience is causal or due to random fluctuations
statements.context: Closing sentence of a guest post by 'Alex' (Alex Mendelsohn, PhD, UK physicist) arguing that Poisson clumping biases psychiatrists' prescribing (his example: pregabalin for GAD). He suggests teaching randomness in psychiatric education could reduce this bias.
statements.note: Guest author's hedged claim; the author thanks him but does not restate or endorse the specific claim. Weak predictive reading.

statements.quote: These promising findings represent a major step forward in our goal to bring a paradigm-shifting treatment to the millions of patients who are profoundly impacted by GAD
statements.context: Pasted MindMed press release on MM-120 (LSD analog) phase IIb data in generalized anxiety disorder: 7.6-point HAM-A reduction vs placebo at week 4, Cohen's d 0.88. Quote is from CEO Robert Barrow. The author calls the data 'groundbreaking' but adds no forecast of his own.
statements.note: Quoted third-party press release; a goal statement rather than a dated forecast.

statements.quote: I'm going to get back to it now because I need to.
statements.context: The author is senior author on a series of eight academic papers; seven are submitted and under review, and he is responsible for finishing the last one. He frames the newsletter post as ADHD avoidance and commits to returning to the paper.
statements.note: Trivial personal commitment; no claim about when the paper series will be finished or published.

statements.quote: as of 2024, The Joint Commission has decided that patient suicide is a sentinel event
statements.context: Regulatory update post. The author reports that from 2024 The Joint Commission will count a death by suicide as a sentinel event if it occurs in a healthcare setting or within seven days of discharge from inpatient, emergency department, intensive outpatient, residential, group home or transitional living settings, replacing the prior 72-hour window.
statements.note: Restatement of an announced policy that takes effect after the post date; near-certain, not an author prediction.

statements.quote: This is also going to be a huge pain in the neck for individuals working in those settings, because more suicides will be a big deal.
statements.context: Author's expectation about the effect of The Joint Commission's 2024 sentinel-event rule on staff in inpatient, emergency, residential and intensive outpatient settings: more post-discharge suicides will count and be scrutinized.
statements.note: Implied horizon is 2024 when the rule takes effect.

statements.quote: However, making it something we have to follow up on, something we have to report on, and some hospitals are graded on, and audited for brings an entire new level of seriousness to post-discharge suicide and its follow up.
statements.context: Author's claim that mandatory reporting, grading and auditing under the 2024 Joint Commission sentinel-event rule will raise the seriousness with which hospitals treat post-discharge suicide and follow-up.
statements.note: Present-tense assertion about a consequence of a rule that has not yet taken effect; borderline.

statements.quote: Honestly, I hope the numbers are as sobering as I fear they will be. And I hope they push us towards more effective treatments, like SAINT neuromodulation , Esketamine, and other rapid-acting therapeutics.
statements.context: Author expects that once post-discharge suicides are counted as sentinel events from 2024, the counts will be sobering (high), and hopes this pushes the field toward SAINT neuromodulation, esketamine and other rapid-acting treatments.
statements.note: Compound: a fear-based expectation about the counted numbers plus a hope about treatment adoption. The hope has no predictive reading on its own.

statements.quote: 60% of adults plan to have a casual sexual encounter during the holidays
statements.context: The author dissects a Yahoo Life story built on an EverlyWell (STI testing company) sponsored 'Hometown Holiday Hook-Up Survey' claiming 60% of adults plan a casual sexual encounter over the 2023 holidays. He calls it clickbait and sponsored content, and argues the real story is loneliness.
statements.note: Third-party survey claim that the author mocks and does not adopt.

statements.quote: There is a risk of never having the kind of social life that might lead to a sexual encounter, awkwardly, in the back of a car, perhaps rented from Zipcar.
statements.context: After citing CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey data (ever sexually active high schoolers: 54% in 1991, 46% in 2009, 30% in 2021), the author argues young people's ability to connect has collapsed and frames the risk of never developing a social life as a new youth risk.
statements.note: Borderline: a risk statement about a cohort's future rather than a dated call.

statements.quote: If you enjou these topics, and will be in the San Fransisco Area on January 7th, please join us for Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment, 2024!
statements.context: Closing invitation in a podcast guest-appearance blurb. The author announces the Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment 2024 live event in the San Francisco area on January 7 (2024) with tickets on sale; RAMHT is the author's own conference.
statements.note: Event announcement for the author's own organization (RAMHT); coder may mark CONTROL. Typos 'enjou' and 'Fransisco' are in the source.

statements.quote: Compass Pathways is the biotech company bringing its psilocybin analog, Comp360, to market.
statements.context: Setup sentence introducing Compass Pathways and COMP360 before the author discusses the PTSD study (single 25mg dose, no serious treatment-emergent adverse events) and the NEJM phase 2b treatment-resistant depression data (29.1% remission at week 3).
statements.note: Descriptive present progressive that implies eventual market entry; borderline.

statements.quote: There is still a lot of research to be done before these become well-established medicines.
statements.context: After arguing that COMP360's phase 2b TRD result (29.1% remission at week 3, p<0.002) shows a phase-3-sized difference in a phase-2-sized trial, the author tempers expectations: psilocybin-class drugs will need much more research before becoming established medicines for depression and PTSD.
statements.confidence_phrase: still a lot of research to be done
statements.note: Implies eventual establishment but with a substantial delay; no date.

statements.quote: I look forward to the kinds of risk mitigation measures needed to reduce harm to humans with serious health conditions.
statements.context: Author anticipates that psilocybin-class treatments such as COMP360 for depression and PTSD will come with risk mitigation measures (REMS-style safeguards) to reduce harm to patients with serious health conditions.
statements.note: Expectation framed as anticipation; implies approval with risk mitigation requirements.

statements.quote: But this Christmas, I am hopeful we will have new and powerful treatments for depression under the tree in the near future!
statements.context: Closing line of the Christmas-day post on Compass Pathways COMP360 phase 2b data. The author expects new, powerful depression treatments (psilocybin-class) to arrive in the near future.
statements.confidence_phrase: I am hopeful we will have
statements.note: Hope-framed but carries 'we will have' plus a time phrase.

statements.quote: Very shortly, I hope our hospitals can include SAINT , if not angels, and other rapid-acting treatments.
statements.context: Essay on It's a Wonderful Life and suicide risk assessment (Tyler Black on the Psychiatry Boost Camp podcast; Joiner's interpersonal model). The author says suicidal crises can usually be handled without hospitalization and hopes hospitals will soon offer SAINT neuromodulation and other rapid-acting treatments.
statements.note: Hope-framed; logged because of the explicit time word. Author has commercial ties to SAINT-related ventures.

statements.quote: I’m hosting a conference on the topic in a few weeks —Jan 7th.
statements.context: The author links the paranormal perspective shift in It's a Wonderful Life to his prior-day column on psilocybin for PTSD and announces he is hosting a conference on rapid-acting treatments on January 7 (2024), the RAMHT event.
statements.note: Event announcement for the author's own organization; repeats the planetary-intergalactic announcement.
